input.subject: Washing machine – Flat 15, 55 Alder Lane (Ref R/PM040-1) – please confirm next step
input.body:
Hello,

Thank you for confirming you are happy for someone to check the washing machine at Flat 15, 55 Alder Lane, Northbridge, ZZ1 6ZZ (Ref R/PM040-1).

Shortly before your reply, the tenant let us know they have swapped in their own washing machine themselves and stored your faulty machine in the garage, as they are going away on holiday soon.

As the situation has changed, could you confirm how you would like us to proceed:
1. Still send an engineer to inspect/repair your machine (now in the garage), or
2. Leave things as they are for now, with your machine stored in the garage.

Please note the tenant mentioned there are no isolation valves on the water pipes; you may wish an engineer to check the connections of the replacement machine at the same visit.

We won't book anyone until we hear back from you.

Kind regards,
Donna
Northbridge Lettings

input.body:
Hello,

Thank you for letting us know you have swapped in your own washing machine and stored the original in the garage at Flat 15, 55 Alder Lane (Ref R/PM040-1).

The landlord had also said they are happy for an engineer to look at the original machine, so we are checking with them whether they still want this. If they do, we'll need to arrange access around your holiday. Could you let us know the dates you will be away and whether the garage can be accessed while you're gone?

In the meantime, please keep an eye on the pipe connections behind your machine for any leaks, and let us know straight away if you notice any. We will be back in touch by 31 December.

Kind regards,
Donna
Northbridge Lettings

result.summary: I recorded the landlord's approval for an engineer to check the washing machine. I haven't booked anyone yet, because the tenant had already swapped in their own machine and put the faulty one in the garage, and the landlord's reply doesn't mention the swap. I've emailed the landlord to ask whether they still want their machine inspected, and asked the tenant for their holiday dates and whether the garage can be reached while they're away. The case is on hold with a follow-up in 7 days.

judgement.why_this_decision: Event 009 is a clear go-ahead for an engineer to attend (classifier: approve 0.98), so I recorded approval 37 as approved. But event 008, sent 25 minutes earlier, says the tenant swapped machines and stored the faulty one in the garage because they are leaving on holiday soon. That changes what the visit is for and makes access uncertain. The landlord's reply doesn't mention the swap. There is also no contractor on the ticket and no job history at this property, so I had no contractor to assign. Asking the landlord and tenant one question each is quicker and cheaper than booking a visit that may not be wanted or may not get in.

alternatives_considered.why_not: There is no contractor on record or in the property history. The faulty machine is now in the garage and the tenant is going away, so the landlord may not want a visit and access may not work.

alternatives_considered.option: Close the ticket as resolved by the tenant
alternatives_considered.why_not: The landlord's machine is still faulty and the landlord has asked for it to be checked. Closing would ignore what the landlord said.
Nothing here is a real conflict, a cost dispute or a safety emergency. The landlord and tenant can answer the open questions themselves.
